checks.claim: Source page 5 (1.20) heat normalization; page 13 (2.24) Laplace cap and spatial Gaussian convolution; Green regularization; fit with manuscript multiplier-in-[0,1], nested Laplace domains, and N0 mass
checks.reason: (1.20) prints p(t,x)=(2 pi t)^{-d/2} exp(-|x|^2/(2t)), the probability-normalized Brownian heat kernel. (2.24) prints gamma^0_delta(u)=Gamma(alpha0)^{-1} integral_0^{delta^{-1}} e^{-lambda|u|} dlambda/lambda^{1-alpha0} (cap delta^{-1} confirmed in crop) and gamma_epsilon = gamma * p_epsilon. Page 13's G_eta(t,x)=integral_{R^3} p(eta,x-y)G(t,y)dy is normalized spatial heat convolution. Manuscript fit holds: spatial and Green Gaussian smoothing give Fourier multipliers in [0,1]; the manuscript's measurable nested S subset S' subset (0,infinity) Laplace domains mirror source (3.2)'s measurable A_{j,k} and the (2.24) cap; the N0 mass identity G_s(R^d)=s (giving N0(theta)=theta^{-2}) is preserved by the normalized heat convolution, as the manuscript separately asserts. The manuscript explicitly declines a homogeneous model for arbitrary multipliers: 'An arbitrary m need not preserve Hypothesis 1.2.1; the scaling identities above are asserted for the original covariance only' (page 29).

checks.claim: Source page 14 (3.3)-(3.5) shapes and variables versus the manuscript's explicit reading
checks.reason: (3.3) index-free mass norm matches manuscript N0 shape; (3.4) Gamma(alpha0)^{-1} |time-Laplace/space-Fourier transform of G| dlambda/lambda^{1-alpha0} mu(d xi) matches N1 via the wave Laplace transform 1/((theta+lambda)^2+|xi|^2), which is real positive so the printed modulus is transparent. Native-resolution crop of (3.5) confirms the printed formula has both Green factors with the same spatial variable: G(s,x)G(t,x), with y appearing only in gamma_{j,k}(x-y) and dy. The manuscript does not silently attribute the corrected formula: page 28 states 'the second Green factor in the printed source (3.5) is read with the independent variable y; see Lemma 2.3.2 and Remark 2.3.3 for the independent justification and the exact source qualification.' It also states the bounds are derived directly ('we use the norms in the source's (3.3)-(3.5)... but give their bounds directly'), so no proof of Chen's general pairing theorem is imported or certified.
